updates.assessment: Manual export retains atomic copies and sidecar routing, reports progress, and moves only fully completed file-and-sidecar predecessors to trash after an export failure. Cancellation before the deletion phase—including after the final copy—suppresses all trashing. Confirmed cleanup uses combined-local deletion in64-record chunks, so archived-file physical delete lock does not block moving files to trash. Sidecar failure prevents that file copy and excludes it from the completed prefix. Later cleanup failure retains earlier committed counts and the original export diagnostic; completion refreshes the owner while failure details remain available.
limitations: Exactly one original export-worker leaf; manual-export parent, filename controls and tag-sidebar gaps remain separately assessed. No native-ID completion credit.

Native source/path/symlink preflight precedes sidecars and is stricter than Qt. Atomic destination replacement and hardlink protection remain intentional differences; filesystem artifact ordering is not wholly identical.

Native progress and error details remain in the review window rather than Qt job popup/critical dialog. Failed or cancelled Export-and-close stays open natively; Qt closes its review frame after worker completion.

Qt blocks its worker on critical-error acknowledgement before prefix cleanup, allowing cancellation during that pause. Native reports the error inline and may immediately begin already-confirmed cleanup, with no modal acknowledgement gate. The recorder intercepts ShowCritical and does not validate acknowledgement timing.
Cancellation is sampled between files and once before deletion; it does not roll back completed copies or cancel already-authorized deletion chunks. Sidecars can remain after a later copy failure.
Native cleanup exceptions preserve the original export error and count of earlier committed chunks instead of leaving an unhandled worker exception.

Six actual Qt cases cover success, first/later missing-source failure, second sidecar failure and cancellation after first/final copy with archived delete lock enabled and post-shutdown SQLite membership. The64-record boundary is directly source-traced and exercised by a native66-file/second-transaction-failure regression, not a65-file Qt recording.
GUI evidence is callback-driven confirmation/worker/refresh behavior; no physical pointer parity claim. Reference PNG shows the panel after error capture, not the intercepted critical dialog.
Exact-source full Linux validation and independent native rendered review passed. Windows/macOS remain deferred.
